title: Programmatic SEO Services Done Responsibly | Elevate Aura
meta: Programmatic SEO services: real search intent, unique data per page, templates and internal links, 50 to 250 pages per product and city, no doorway pages.
h1: Programmatic SEO services, with the doorway pages left out.
sub: Generating hundreds of pages is easy and usually a mistake. Doing it well means proving the demand, holding unique data for every page, designing a template that reads like a page a person wanted, and refusing the pages that fail those tests.

Unique data per page or no page
whatsapp_text: Hi, I'd like to discuss programmatic SEO for our catalogue.
persona: Marketing lead at a business with a large catalogue or a wide service territory

paras: Programmatic SEO is building a set of pages from a data source and a template instead of writing each one by hand. It suits businesses with structured repetition: a product in a city, a model in an application, a service at a branch. Done properly it gives a searcher exactly the page they asked for. Done badly it produces hundreds of near-identical pages that search engines call doorway pages and treat accordingly.

The difference is entirely in the data. If each page carries something genuinely different, a specification, a real application note, an actual service reach or a real price band, it is a page. If the only variable is a city name dropped into the same sentences, it is not, and we will not build it.

The site describes this work as 50 to 250 pages per product and city. Elevate Aura built 253 product and city landing pages across four product lines for Medline Robotics, a medical robotics company in Chennai.

sections.h2: Five hundred pages that all say the same thing.
sections.lead: Most failed programmatic projects fail the same way, and the failure is visible before a single page is published.

items.p: The same text with a place name substituted. A searcher recognises it instantly, and so does a search engine.
Pages built for combinations nobody searches, filling the site with content that can never earn a visit.

items.h: Claims that are not true locally
items.p: A page implying an office or same-day service in a city where the business has neither.
Hundreds of orphan pages with nothing linking to them, so most are never crawled properly.

sections.eyebrow: How we build a page set
sections.h2: Six checks before a set goes live.

steps.p: Each combination is checked for real search demand. Combinations without it are dropped from the plan, not padded out.
Every page must carry something true and specific to it. If the data does not exist, the page is not built.
A layout that reads as a deliberate page: heading, the specific data, the differences that matter and a clear next step.
Sections that only apply to some pages appear only on those pages, rather than being filled with filler text everywhere.
Category hubs, breadcrumbs and sideways links between related pages, so nothing is an orphan.
After the set has been indexed, pages that attract nothing are rewritten or removed, and the finding shapes the next set.

items: Source data audited from your systems

sections.h2: Where a page set earns its keep.

items.h: A catalogue with four product lines
items.workflow: Each model gets a specification page, each application an explainer, and the cities actually supplied get pages describing delivery, installation and service reach.
items.result: The Medline Robotics pattern: 253 pages across four lines.

items.workflow: Only the towns where engineers genuinely travel get pages, each stating the honest travel position rather than implying a branch.

items.h: A set that should not be built
items.workflow: Research shows no demand for a model-and-city combination and no data to distinguish the pages from each other.
items.result: We say so and the budget goes to pages that can work.

items.q: How many pages will you build for us?
items.a: Typically 50 to 250 per product and city programme, decided after the demand research. Medline Robotics ended at 253 across four product lines. The number is an outcome of the data, never a target agreed in advance.

items.q: Are programmatic pages against search engine guidelines?
items.a: Pages built from data to serve a real search are not. Doorway pages, meaning near-identical pages made only to funnel visitors, are. The difference is whether each page carries something genuinely unique, which is why we test that first.

items.q: Will you build city pages for cities where we have no office?
items.a: Only if the page says honestly what you do there. For Elevate Aura that means setup is remote and support is on WhatsApp, with in-person work in Chennai. We will write the same honest position for you, not imply a branch.

items.q: What if our data is not good enough?
items.a: Then we fix the data before building pages, or we do not build the set. A catalogue with no specification fields cannot produce distinguishable pages, so the first job is structuring it. See catalogue website development.
The pages are generated from your data through templates, and the written sections are drafted and edited by a person against that data. Nothing is published that neither of us has read.

items.q: What happens to pages that never attract anyone?
items.a: They are reviewed after indexing and either rewritten with better data or removed. Leaving dead pages on a site helps nobody, and pruning is written into the engagement rather than left as an optional extra.
